analysis:
Examined the StartupPreloader summary additions, the new status-command lines and the new tests. StartupPreloader.swift adds two summary fields, `failedInsufficientMemory` (line 137) and `notAttempted` (line 139), populated at lines 159-162 and 203-206. These are in-process bookkeeping only and do not change admission, load, self-test or retire logic. Memory admission stays non-evicting, and the fail-open and fail-closed self-test behavior is unchanged. The change does not touch the wire protocol, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or the add-on hold socket (TB-012).

StatusCommand+Residency.swift adds `pendingSelectionLines` and `recoveryLines`, and StatusCommand.swift calls them (lines 155 and 178). Both are read-only CLI renderers of the owner-only daemon state file (`enabledModelsAtLastSwitch`, `enabledModelsAtStart`, `selectedModelRecovery`). They output model IDs, memory figures and an optional `blocker` string.

The `blocker` text is printed verbatim to the local terminal, so control characters in the state file could in principle reach it. The file is written by the daemon and is owner-only, so a same-user attacker already has equivalent access. Output is not sent to the coordinator or to consumers. I see no new trust-boundary crossing.

The new tests run in a sandbox and only check output text. Unverified, outside the supplied evidence: how the daemon populates `selected_model_recovery` and `blocker`, and whether that text can include prompt-derived or other sensitive data. The units shown suggest only model IDs and memory numbers. A reviewer of the daemon-side writer should confirm this. The `[Self.glmID]` test fixtures are benign.

No findings. The state-file origin of the fields and the daemon-side writer are unverified, so deeper review is not required unless that writer is in scope.
